notes: Task 12 (EE2ComplianceTools, Phase B8) from .kiro/specs/python-mcp-server-port/tasks.md. Ports the 5 Node.js EE2ComplianceTools to Python. SME-corrected behaviour (set -eu is NOT required; err_chk/err_exit is the correct pattern; 80% false positive on set -eu) must be preserved. The 4 content-scanning tools are content-abstracted: the Python port rejects repository_path / path arguments with a clear [ERROR] instructing the caller to use content / files — the tools never read from disk. search_ee2_standards is the only vector-backed tool; the other 4 are pure content-scanners that work in degraded mode.

scan_repository_compliance environment_variables category is intentionally no-op in the Node.js port — only Phase-2-validated rules fire, and that category has no configured rules (`anti_patterns.environment_variables` is empty). The Python port preserves this behaviour for parity; if SMEs later add environment-variable rules to the Phase 2 annotations, the scan tool will need a second pass to wire up the pattern execution path.

extract_code_for_analysis `path` mode is rejected by the Python port. If a future phase wants local-filesystem scanning from the hosted runtime (e.g. for an HPC-researcher use case where the MCP server is co-located with the source tree), port CodeSnippetExtractor.extractFromDirectory and gate it behind an env var. Until then, callers must pass content/files arrays.
